2  THIS APPEAL HAVING BEEN RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT ON 11.09.2024 COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT, THIS DAY,
VIJAYKUMAR A. PATIL J., DELIVERED/PRONOUNCED THE FOLLOWING:
CORAM:
HON'BLE
MR. JUSTICE KRISHNA S.DIXIT
AND  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIJAYKUMAR A.PATIL  CAV JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE VIJAYKUMAR A. PATIL)

This appeal is filed by the injured seeking for higher compensation being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 09.11.2018 passed in MVC No.1864/2017 by the XI Addl. District Judge & Addl. MACT., Belagavi.

entities.text: XI Addl. District Judge & Addl. MACT., Belagavi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Brief facts are that on 08.07.2017 the appellant was proceeding on a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA- 22/EL-6325, at that time, a car bearing registration No.KA- 26/M-4943 came from Belagavi side to Khanapur, driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the above said motorcycle which resulted in accident.

The appellant sustained grievous injuries,
provided treatment as inpatient from 08.07.2017 to 19.07.2017 and suffered physical disability.
He filed the claim petition before the Tribunal seeking compensation.
3. The respondents entered appearance before the Tribunal and opposed the claim petition by denying the accident, nature of injuries, age, income and avocation of the claimant.
They sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
4. The Tribunal recorded the evidence of the parties.
The claimant examined himself as PW1 and examined Dr.S.R.Angadi as PW2, got marked Exs.P1 to P18.
The respondents did not adduce any evidence.
The Tribunal has awarded total compensation of Rs.10,40,100/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.
Being aggrieved by the same, the claimant is in appeal.
5. Sri.Harish S.Maigur, learned counsel appearing for the claimant submits that the Tribunal has committed error in awarding compensation under the head of medical expenses on lower side.
It is submitted that the Tribunal has committed further error in assessing disability at 33% which is contrary to the evidence of PW2.

He submits that the income of the appellant is required to be re-assessed as he was working as a Turner and earning Rs.15,000/- per month and due to the Shri.Uttam Vithal Goral vs Shri.Uday A Raikar on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198210472/
2 accident, he is unable to perform the said work.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is also submitted that the appellant is entitled compensation under the head of loss of future prospects as he has suffered disability more than 50%
to whole body.
It is contended that the award of compensation on all other heads is required to be re-assessed appropriately.
6. Per contra, Sri.S.K.Kayakmath and Sri.M.Y.Katagi, learned counsel appearing for the contesting respondents support the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal.
It is submitted that the Tribunal considering the bills produced, has awarded just and fair compensation under the head of Medical expenses.
It is further submitted that PW2 is not a treated Doctor and he is considered as a Stock Doctor to give evidence in motor vehicle accident cases, hence, his evidence is not worthy to be believed.
It is also submitted that the appellant has not placed any evidence to substantiate the claim for compensation under the head of loss of future prospects.
Thus, they seek to dismiss the appeal.
7. We have heard the arguments of the learned counsel appearing for the parties, perused the memorandum of appeal and the Tribunal records.
The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal calls for any interference?
8. The undisputed facts are that the appellant met with a road accident on 08.07.2017 and sustained following injuries and fractures:
"1) Contested abrasion present over left side of forehead.
2) Mucosal laceration over upper lip.
3) Swelling with deformity and punctured wound present over distal 1/3 of right leg.
Abnormal mobility present.
4) Swelling with abnormal mobility over proximal 1/3rd and distal 1/3rd of left leg.
X-ray: Chest-> AP ... nothing significant.
Pelvis with both hips-AP.. nothing significant.
Left leg with ankle..
AP lat...
Segmental tibia and fibula fracture
Left knee with ankle..
AP Lat...
Segmental tibia and fibula fracture
Right leg with ankle..
AP lat...
Distal 1/3 tibia and fibula fracture Right leg and knee...
AP lat...
Distal 1/3 tibia and fibula fracture Left foot...

AP oblique... Nothing significant MRI:
Brain and cervical spine with screening of whole spine-C3- C4 and C4-C5 and C5-C6 diffuse disc bridge L3-L4 and L4-L5 mild diffuse bulge."
9.
Admittedly, PW2 is not a treated Doctor to the appellant and no explanation is offered by the appellant as to why the treated Doctor has not been examined before the Tribunal.
The evidence of PW2 indicates that the appellant has sustained 10% permanent disability due to cervical spine injury which is assessed as a whole body disability.
PW2 further assessed permanent physical disability to the extent of 35% due to Type-I compound fracture distal 1/3rd of right tibia and fibula bones.
He further assessed disability to the extent of 35% to the left ankle joint due to segmental Shri.
Uttam Vithal Goral vs Shri.Uday A Raikar on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198210472/

entities.text: Uttam Vithal Goral vs Shri.Uday A Raikar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3 fracture of left tibia and fibula bones.
The evidence on record indicates that due to the fractures referred supra implants were inserted in his right and left ankle joints and there is deformity in the joints.
The evidence of PW2 as it is cannot be accepted for the simple reason that he is not a treated Doctor nor he assigned any reason for arriving at such a conclusion for disability.

Considering the Wound Certificate at Ex.P6, oral testimony of PW2, Discharge Summary at Ex.P7 and other records like MRI Report, X-Ray Report and Disability Certificate at Ex.P10, we are of the considered view that it would be just and appropriate to re-assess the disability at 40% to the whole body for the purpose of determination of compensation.
10. The Tribunal has assessed the income of the injured at Rs.10,000/- per month which is required to be re- assessed.
Accordingly, we re-
assess the same at Rs.10,250/- per month placing reliance on the notional income chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The appellant has not produced any evidence before the Tribunal with regard to the claim for loss of future prospects.

The evidence does not indicate that the appellant is unable to carry out any work due to the disability suffered by him in the road accident and in the absence of any evidence, we are unable to accept the claim of the appellant with regard to entitlement of compensation under the head of loss of future prospects.
There is no dispute with regard to application of multiplier of 16.

Thus, the claimant is entitled to modified compensation on the head of loss of future earnings due to disability as under:
Rs.10,250 x 12 x 16 x 40/100 = Rs.7,87,200/-
11.

The Tribunal has awarded Rs.2,50,500/- under the head of Medical Expenses by considering the bills and proof of expenditure incurred by the claimant under the said head, we do not propose to alter the same in the absence of any evidence for higher claim.
12. The appellant was inpatient for 12 days, has undergone surgery and implants were inserted hence, award of compensation on conventional heads is required to be enhanced appropriately.

Thus, the compensation is re- assessed as under:
 Pain and suffering Rs. 75,000/-

Medical expenses Rs.2,50,500/-
Food, nourishment charges, attendant & travelling expenses Rs. 25,000/-
 Loss of future earning Rs.7,87,200/-
 Loss of income during laid-up period Rs. 41,000/-
 Loss of amenities Rs. 50,000/-
 ------------------
 Total Rs.12,28,700/-
 ------------------
 13.
In all, the claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.12,28,700/- as against Rs.10,40,100/- awarded by the Tribunal.

sentences.text:
In the result, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER a) The appeal stands partly allowed.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that the claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.12,28,700/- as against Rs.10,40,100/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
d) The respondent No.2/insurer shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
e) On such deposit, the same shall be released in favour of the appellant.
f) Draw modified award accordingly.
g) No order as to costs.

Sd/-
